notes: Covers the Archer C7 hardware version 2 (FCC TE7C7V2, approved April 2014 per DeviWiki). Other hardware versions can differ: TP-Link's product page for the V5 lists a 12 V 1.5 A adapter, and SmallNetBuilder says v2 changed the 5 GHz radio chip and the flash size compared with v1.

gaps: Flash conflict: SmallNetBuilder's table names Winbond W25Q64FV (the cell also shows 16 MB and 8 MB), but its update text says v2 flash rose from 8 MB to 16 MB.
DeviWiki gives Winbond W25Q128FV, 16 MiB. Each flash name is recorded as its own source gives it; not resolved, so check the board.

5 GHz power amplifiers: SmallNetBuilder's table says SiGE 5005L (x3); DeviWiki's additional-chips field says Skyworks SE5003L1 (marking 5003L1, x3), though DeviWiki's own comparison table repeats 5005L for v2.
eeworldonline's teardown (hardware version not stated) says three Skyworks power amplifiers sit on the 5 GHz board, with no part number. The amplifier conflict is not resolved.
RAM: SmallNetBuilder says Winbond W9751G6JB (x2); DeviWiki's RAM1 field says W9751G6KB-25 (x2) while its summary block says W9751G6JB. Not resolved.

Adapter: 12 VDC 2.5 A rests on DeviWiki's v2 page and an OpenWrt forum poster who says his v2 is rated 12V 2.5A. TP-Link's product page covers the V5 (12 V 1.5 A), so it is not used for the rating. No adapter label was read.
The three 2.4 GHz power amplifiers are listed only as unidentified, so they are not claimed.
Ethernet switch: AR8327N (DeviWiki's switch field) or AR8327 (DeviWiki's text and SmallNetBuilder's table). No part type in the guide fits a switch chip, so it is not claimed.
SoC and RAM names rest on SmallNetBuilder and DeviWiki text, not on the FCC internal photos, whose chip markings the researcher found illegible (the photos could not be opened by the checker).
Production years: none of the sources read gives them.

The FCC user manual and exhibit pages on fccid.io returned HTTP 403, so the antenna, LED and port claims were re-sourced to TP-Link's own V2.0 user guide (REV4.0.2, the revision the researcher read on the FCC site).
The LCSC datasheet link (lcsc.com/datasheet/C571265.pdf) returns an HTML page, not a PDF, so it is not cited; the LCSC listing for the W25Q128FVSIG is cited instead.
method: SmallNetBuilder's TP-LINK Archer C7 V2 review: Table 1 (single V2 column) and the text on the v1-to-v2 changes (5 GHz radio, flash).
DeviWiki page for the TP-Link Archer C7 v2 (community wiki, readable without a bot check): CPU, flash, RAM, switch, power, ports, antenna connectors, additional chips, FCC ID.

TP-Link's Archer C7(US) V 2.0 user guide, REV4.0.2 (static.tp-link.com, linked from TP-Link's V2 download page): LED table on printed pages 4-5, rear panel on pages 5-6, Appendix C specifications on page 128.
OpenWrt forum thread on the Archer C7 adapter (March 2018): the poster says his v2 is rated 12V 2.5A. Community source.
TP-Link's Archer C7 product page shows the V5 only, so it is used for the V5 adapter rating in the notes.
eeworldonline teardown of an Archer C7 (hardware version not stated): names QCA9558, AR8327, Winbond DDR2 and Skyworks 5 GHz amplifiers; not cited for parts.
LCSC listing for the Winbond W25Q128FVSIG (C571265): lists it as a 128 Mbit SPI NOR flash.
Refused or unreadable: fccid.io device page, user manual and internal photos for TE7C7V2 (HTTP 403 to the checker).
Refused to the researcher: openwrt.org Table of Hardware and techinfodepot.shoutwiki.com (Anubis bot checks), fcc.report exhibits (HTTP 403).

comps.spec: Qualcomm Atheros QCA9558 SoC, dual-band 3-stream 802.11n; the 2.4 GHz radio is inside this chip (SmallNetBuilder table). DeviWiki gives the CPU clock as 720 MHz
Qualcomm Atheros QCA9880-BR4A 3x3 802.11ac 5 GHz radio; the v2 part (v1 used QCA9880-AR1A)
Three 5 GHz RF power amplifiers. SmallNetBuilder's table lists them as SiGE 5005L; DeviWiki's additional-chips field instead names Skyworks SE5003L1 (marking 5003L1). The sources disagree
Three detachable 5 GHz antennas on RP-SMA connectors, 5 dBi; the three 2.4 GHz antennas are internal (TP-Link V2.0 user guide, specifications)
DC power adapter, 12 V 2.5 A, barrel connector (DeviWiki's v2 page; an OpenWrt forum poster also gives 12V 2.5A for his v2)
Front-panel LEDs: Power, System, Wireless 2.4GHz, Wireless 5GHz, Ethernet, Internet and WPS; one USB LED on the rear panel
Gigabit RJ-45 ports: one Internet (WAN) and four Ethernet (LAN); two USB ports; power socket on the rear panel
Two Winbond W9751G6JB DDR2 chips, 128 MB total (SmallNetBuilder). DeviWiki's RAM1 field names W9751G6KB-25 and its summary block W9751G6JB
Winbond W25Q128FV flash, 16 MiB (DeviWiki); LCSC lists the W25Q128FVSIG as a 128 Mbit SPI NOR flash. SmallNetBuilder's table names W25Q64FV and its text says 16 MB for v2
